name: Tirta Empul spring dam
summary: A dam at the Tirta Empul spring in Bali, recorded in the tenth-century Manukaya inscription as repaired after repeated flood damage.
description: A dam at the Tirta Empul spring repaired after recurrent flood damage, according to the Manukaya inscription.
tier_reason: A particular dam repair is fine detail; it is not identical to the irrigation practice merely because both appear in one inscription. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: One dam at one spring in a well-watered place, repaired after floods, improving local water control by a known method with no known successors.

why: Recurrent floods damaged the spring dam, so it had to be repaired to keep the water supply working.

date.label: by c. 1000 CE
date.basis: The cited study dates the inscription to 960 CE; a late-tenth-century bound avoids overstating a disputed exact conversion.

events.statement: A spring dam at Tirta Empul was repaired in the tenth-century inscription’s account.
events.population: People maintaining and using the Tirta Empul waterworks
events.caveats: The inscription is read through a modern academic study; exact year conversions and the earlier construction date are uncertain. Repair indicates a pre-existing configuration but does not show continuous use.

evidence.supports: The study reports a tenth-century repair of the Tirta Empul dam and irrigation use of the spring water.
